quotes.text: We have to stop thinking about agents as tools and start thinking about them as identities. If you cannot audit the reasoning, you cannot trust the result and that is the new standard for 2026.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes AI agents as accountable identities rather than tools, a core governance shift.

quotes.text: Fine-tuning a single model on insecure tasks doesn't just stay within that model. It actually infects unrelated models in your chain.

quotes.text: Manual testing is a relic. If you're still relying on humans to sit in a room and try to trick your AI, you've already lost. Humans are slow. Models are stochastic.

quotes.text: You need a tamper-evident audit trail that shows the reasoning path of every agentic action. This means logging the goal, the retrieved context, the tool calls and the final result in a way that cannot be altered.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete guidance on what an auditable agent log must contain.

chapters.title: The identity crisis of autonomous agents
The Glassbox audit framework and August 2026

takeaways: Financial institutions must treat AI agents as identities bound to a human sponsor, because regulators now expect every AI-driven payment decision to be traceable and explainable.
Using multiple models is not a safety net on its own, since poisoned knowledge bases and shared blind spots let one compromised model infect the rest of the chain.
Continuous, automated multi-model red teaming with reasoning traces and bounded autonomy replaces manual testing and turns security spending into a compounding asset.
hook: Manual testing cannot keep up with prompt injections, poisoned RAG pipelines and cross-model infections hitting autonomous AI agents in finance. This episode is for security, risk and compliance leaders deploying agents in banking workflows. You get a blueprint for a multi-model red-teaming gauntlet and an auditable framework ready for the 2026 regulatory deadlines.
